headline: HLA and TCR-pMHC context enter immune repertoire and viral sequence simulation
label: Immune Sequence Simulation Frameworks
summary: Simulators and structure-based recognition models now encode host HLA and epitope constraints, and AIRR-seq simulators are being benchmarked against one…
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational modeling of immune and viral sequences under host immune constraints, although the items differ in scope. UnivAIRRse provides a unified five-level framework, with a web explorer, for comparing AIRR-seq repertoire simulators by assumptions, scope and abstraction level. wavess 1.2 adds an explicit HLA-aware CTL response and a method for identifying HLA-specific epitopes to within-host virus sequence simulation. Structure-based work addresses TCR-pMHC binding: a GNN classifier trained on predicted structures is assessed for generalization to unseen peptides, and TCRLens applies equivariant graph learning with VAE-GAN augmentation to TCR-pMHC-I recognition and immunogenic epitope discovery. A protein language model fine-tuned on generated CAR sequences predicts CAR-T cytotoxicity with experimental validation. What is new is explicit HLA context entering simulation of immune and viral sequence evolution, alongside structure-aware prediction of recognition.
